title: Principality of Lichtenberg
capsule: The Principality of Lichtenberg was a small German state centred on the Nahe River valley in the Hunsrück region, constituted in 1815 as an exclave of the Duchy of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld from territories assigned to that house at the Congress of Vienna. Duke Ernest I of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld governed it as a reforming prince, introducing a constitution in 1820, but the territory proved administratively awkward as an isolated exclave separated from Coburg by foreign states. Ernest sold the principality to the Kingdom of Prussia in 1834, after which it was incorporated into the Rhine Province.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
